rule.name: Persist Claude conversation events to Kafka
rule.description: Every UserPromptSubmit and Stop hook event MUST publish the raw hook payload to the conversation_log Kafka topic via the local producer sidecar so the consumer can persist the conversation between Claude Code and the Cursor user using Claude Code. This rule implements the publish leg of EPIC-008-F-003-S-002.

rule_statement.statement_body: On every UserPromptSubmit hook event, the raw hook payload MUST be POSTed to http://127.0.0.1:8100/produce within the hook timeout.
On every Stop hook event, the raw hook payload MUST be POSTed to http://127.0.0.1:8100/produce within the hook timeout.
If the sidecar is unreachable, a browser must be invoked and a web page must be popped up filling the entire user screen telling the user that there is a problem.

rule.name: Boot execution on SessionStart and PostCompact
rule.description: Wires the ChatHealthy boot program into the V19 engineering-rules architecture. The boot executable runs on SessionStart and PostCompact: SessionStart fires for new sessions and new logins; PostCompact fires when Claude Code auto-compacts its context. Both events trigger the same boot duties so Claude resumes with fresh conversation context and the business taxonomy regardless of how the session was disrupted. The boot reads the hook payload from stdin and dispatches on hook_event_name. Replaces the legacy direct settings.json wiring of chathealthy_devops_boot.py with rule-dispatched invocation through chathealthy_enforcement_manager.py.

rule_statement.statement_body: On SessionStart and PostCompact, the boot MUST read the 170 most recent utterance documents from MongoDB ClaudeCodeLog.conversation_log_archive, trim each document to {actor, content}, order newest-to-oldest, and emit them as part of the hook's additionalContext so Claude resumes with recent conversation context. If the MongoDB read fails, the boot MUST fail open — log the failure and continue with remaining duties.

On SessionStart and PostCompact, the boot MUST read brain/machine_artifacts/content/agile_backlog.json and emit the business taxonomy as part of the hook's additionalContext: every epic's id, name, and description; every feature's id, name, and description; every story's id and name. Story descriptions, requirements, and tests MUST NOT be emitted.

The boot MUST read the Claude Code hook payload JSON from stdin and dispatch on the hook_event_name field. SessionStart and PostCompact MUST each execute the duties in statements 1 and 2. Any other hook_event_name value MUST be a no-op that exits 0.

chathealthy_devops_boot.py MUST NOT appear directly in .claude/settings.json hooks. It is invoked exclusively via Rule-002 enforcement entries dispatched by chathealthy_enforcement_manager.py. .claude/settings.json registers only the enforcement manager (one entry per hook); the manager loads engineering_rules.json and spawns the matching enforcement workers.

On SessionStart and PostCompact, the boot MUST compare the current line count of %TEMP%/chathealthy_consumer_errors.log to a line-count semaphore at %TEMP%/chathealthy_last_boot_error_line.txt. If the current line count exceeds the semaphore, the boot MUST emit one line to additionalContext naming the file path and the new line range. The boot MUST then update the semaphore to the current line count. If the error file does not exist, the boot MUST treat the line count as 0 and emit nothing.

rule.name: All files added to the local Git repository must be scanned for architectural compliance.
rule.description: All JSONs, code and configuration files must be scanned for compliance. Current scope is to ensure that only permissible references to HTTP can be in our code base and other artifacts, and that all JSONs be validated by standard Python schema mechanisms.

rule_statement.statement_body: Every JSON file under brain/machine_artifacts/content/ MUST validate against the schema referenced by its $schema field.
The schema used to validate a brain JSON MUST have been reviewed and approved by the human operator before that schema is relied upon for validation.
Every text-based file committed to the repository MUST NOT reference an insecure http:// URL unless the specific URL is explicitly listed as permitted on the enforcement entry.
Regular expressions MUST NOT be in ChatHealthy.AI's executable front-end or Pipeline code.

rule.name: Build number, App version and Framework Version management
rule.description: On every git commit that is not part of a deploy pipeline, this rule (a) increments the canonical build number stored in MongoDB by one and (b) pushes the new build value to the running Kafka producer so every subsequent message it publishes carries the correct build stamp without the producer needing to re-read MongoDB. The rule touches only the build field; version and framework identifiers are set by humans through a separate path. The producer's in-memory build value is therefore current by virtue of being pushed, never polled.

rule_statement.statement_body: On every post-commit hook event triggered by a commit that is NOT part of a deploy pipeline, the `build` field of the canonical version document in MongoDB is incremented by exactly one. The `version` and `framework` fields are not touched.

After the Mongo update in Statement 1 completes successfully, the new `build` value is pushed to the running Kafka producer process. The producer updates its in-memory static and uses the new value for all subsequent messages it publishes. If the push fails, the producer continues with its prior cached value; the producer self-corrects on next restart by re-reading from MongoDB.

rule.name: Block tool actions targeting the legacy c:\chatHealthy tree
rule.description: All Claude tool actions (Bash commands, Write, Edit, NotebookEdit) that reference the legacy `{CHATHEALTHY_PROJECT_ROOT}` or `c:\chatHealthy\Resources` tree are denied at the Claude Code permission layer (PreToolUse). Triggered after a Claude session (or code Claude wrote) was found to have recreated the deleted legacy directory tree on 2026-05-02 17:27 UTC and written `{CHATHEALTHY_PROJECT_ROOT}/code/LoadDB.ipynb` 85 minutes after Skip deleted the directory at 16:02:20 UTC. The current project lives at `c:\CHATHealthyLLC` and that root must never be left.

rule_statement.statement_body: Bash command containing the substring `{CHATHEALTHY_PROJECT_ROOT}` or `{CHATHEALTHY_PROJECT_ROOT}` (case-insensitive) MUST be denied at PreToolUse.
Bash command containing the substring `c:/chatHealthy/Resources` or `c:\chatHealthy\Resources` (case-insensitive) MUST be denied at PreToolUse.
Bash command targeting any path under `c:\chatHealthy\` other than `c:\CHATHealthyLLC\` (case-insensitive) MUST be denied at PreToolUse.
Write tool with `file_path` containing the substring `{CHATHEALTHY_PROJECT_ROOT}` or `{CHATHEALTHY_PROJECT_ROOT}` (case-insensitive) MUST be denied at PreToolUse.
Write tool with `file_path` containing the substring `c:/chatHealthy/Resources` or `c:\chatHealthy\Resources` (case-insensitive) MUST be denied at PreToolUse.
Write tool with `file_path` under `c:\chatHealthy\` other than `c:\CHATHealthyLLC\` (case-insensitive) MUST be denied at PreToolUse.
Write tool with `content` containing the substring `{CHATHEALTHY_PROJECT_ROOT}` or `{CHATHEALTHY_PROJECT_ROOT}` (case-insensitive) MUST be denied at PreToolUse.
Edit tool with `file_path` containing the substring `{CHATHEALTHY_PROJECT_ROOT}` or `{CHATHEALTHY_PROJECT_ROOT}` (case-insensitive) MUST be denied at PreToolUse.
Edit tool with `file_path` containing the substring `c:/chatHealthy/Resources` or `c:\chatHealthy\Resources` (case-insensitive) MUST be denied at PreToolUse.
Edit tool with `new_string` containing the substring `{CHATHEALTHY_PROJECT_ROOT}` or `{CHATHEALTHY_PROJECT_ROOT}` (case-insensitive) MUST be denied at PreToolUse.
NotebookEdit tool with `notebook_path` under `c:\chatHealthy\` other than `c:\CHATHealthyLLC\` (case-insensitive) MUST be denied at PreToolUse.

Maintenance obligation: if the legacy tree is renamed, removed, or relocated in the future, the patterns in block_legacy_path_worker.py and the corresponding statements above MUST be updated. Skip will track this explicitly; this statement exists to make the maintenance contract visible.

rule.name: No commit or deploy without explicit human authorization
rule.description: Every `git commit` and every deploy invocation MUST be explicitly authorized by the human operator at the moment it fires. A commit represents a human-vetted release candidate ready for distribution; the `git push` that immediately follows is the network operation completing the commit and is implicit in the commit's authorization — no separate authorization is required to push a freshly authorized commit. Interactive terminals satisfy this with an exact-match APPROVE token typed at a prompt that names the action and its affected artifacts; non-interactive contexts (CI runners, IDE integrations, headless shells) satisfy it with paired environment variables that name who authorized the action. The rule is enforced inside ChatHealthy's engineering-rules manager so it runs before any Anthropic / Claude Code hook for code-control integration ever sees the action.

rule_statement.statement_body: No commit or deploy CAN take place without explicit human authorization. A commit represents a human-vetted release candidate; the push that immediately follows is implicit in the commit's authorization and does not require a separate authorization event. This requirement shall be enforced as part of ChatHealthy's rule enforcement prior to an Anthropic hook for code-control integration.
